BBC, 25 Nov 2026 14:06 GMT

Andy Burnham says he is listening to Wales amid devolution row

Andy Burnham has rejected many of the calls for further powers from the Welsh government

Andy Burnham wearing a suit, shirt and tie, in front of the door of No.10 Downing Street. He is carrying a red folder.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has told MPs he is listening to Wales, a week after he refused to consider substantial further powers for the Senedd.

Two former Welsh Labour first ministers and the Plaid Welsh government complained after the prime minister said he was not persuaded of the case to devolve justice, policing, rail infrastructure or the Crown Estate.

The prime minister said he will \"never completely rule things out\" but said he wanted to work on devolving employment support, where he said there was \"common ground\".

Plaid Cymru's Ann Davies MP said Burnham had \"overruled the mandate given by the people of Wales for more responsibility\" at May's Senedd election.

Davies asked Burnham in Prime Minister's Questions: \"When exactly did you decide Wales is no longer worth listening to?\"

In response, he said: \"I am listening to Wales.

\"I've met the first minister a number of times. I have put on offer on the table of deeper devolution around employment support.

\"Let's work first where we have got a clear case and common ground, so we can get more young people into work and into jobs.

\"I will never completely rule things out, but at this moment in time that is the issue that we should work on.\"

Davies accused Burnham of dismissing the calls of 22 Welsh councils which supported the devolution of the Crown Estate,\"TUC Cymru and two former Welsh Labour First Ministers, Carwyn Jones and Mark Drakeford\".

She said after the session: \"When it comes to England, he believes power should be pushed out of Westminster. When it comes to Wales, he is determined to keep it in.\"

The Welsh government agreed with the UK government on the devolution of employment support funding in March, when Labour were still in charge.

Burnham has encouraged the Welsh and Scottish governments to devolve more power to communities since becoming prime minister.

The Welsh government, led by Plaid, had promised to negotiate further autonomy for Wales as part of its election campaign.

First Minister Rhun ap Iorwerth has demanded a meeting after the letter to him from Burnham was published on Friday.

He accused Burnham of not treating Wales as an equal nation - all the powers requested are available to the Scottish government and parliament.

The requests are also Welsh Labour policy and had been pursued by previous Labour administrations in Cardiff.

Former First Minister Carwyn Jones said he did not know what the letter was meant to achieve: \"We lost a bulk of people to Plaid Cymru.\"

News of the letter was welcomed by former Welsh Reform leader Dan Thomas, who said on X: \"Good! Plaid and Welsh Labour have failed with their existing powers.\"

Darren Millar, Welsh Conservative Senedd leader, said the debate was an \"unnecessary distraction from the real issues residents are facing around the cost of living, the longest NHS waiting lists in Britain, lower educational attainment and stagnating economic growth\".

\"Both governments need to get on with the job,\" he said.

On Tuesday the first minister called for a \"new alliance\" to fight for further powers, following support from the trade union body TUC Cymru.

A passenger on a motorbike pulled off a remarkable one-handed catch after the ball was hit out of the ground for six in the Swat Premier League in Pakistan.

British people, particularly teens and young adults, are having less or no sex compared to past generations, but lots are watching porn and sexting, a major study suggests.

It is the first time The National Survey of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles' (Natsal) research into general public sex lives has asked about online behaviours.

The latest results were published in The Lancet and were based on a survey of 6,700 people aged 16–59 who were selected at random across Britain.

Energy bills will rise by 26% for millions of households in January, the highest rate in nearly four years, after a surge in gas prices sparked by the Iran war.

Isaac, a student at Durham University, said he had no choice but to keep the heating in his student house on 'constantly' due to poor insulation, and he was not looking forward to the price increase.

In the Autumn budget, the government announced a one-off payment of £100 for households in council bands A to D, 'half a weekly shop' according to Isaac.
